purpose: Check current primary or official sources before deciding how THOS should use the v6 x1 JSON Schema contract.

source_notes.use: Keep the schema declared as draft 2020-12 and avoid older draft tuple semantics.
Treat validation as structural constraints only, not as evidence for GMUT physics claims.
Record changed array and dynamic-reference semantics as a compatibility risk for future schemas.
Local environment already has jsonschema 4.26.0; no new dependency was installed.
Confirm Draft202012Validator is the latest validator class in the Python stack.
Record cross-runtime caveat that draft 2020-12 needs a distinct validator mode.
Route future conformance work to an official language-agnostic fixture suite.
Record future cross-implementation reporting route; not required for current local guard.
Keep path checks resolve-based when guarding repo-root escapes.
Keep git probes explicit-argument subprocess calls in validator code.
Future validator reports can map to SARIF, but v6 x2 stays local JSON.
Future provenance can attach signed build claims, but no workflow mutation is made in this phase.
Keep tool-schema thinking compatible with MCP structured output fields.
Treat docs MCP as read-only source access, not an action connector.
Cloud file writes remain blocked until a separate approval scope exists.

decision: Use installed jsonschema as an optional local validator and add no new package, workflow, Drive mutation, or cloud write.
